title: Regular savings: SIPs and annuities
summary: A SIP, an EMI, rent and a pension are all streams of equal payments. FV, PV and PMT handle them with the pmt argument, NPER finds how long, and RATE finds the return a plan really gives.
objectives: Value a stream of equal payments with FV and PV.
Choose type 1 for payments at the start of each period and 0 for the end.
Work out the payment, the time or the rate needed for a goal with PMT, NPER and RATE.
Use RATE to test what a savings plan really earns.

slides.h: An annuity is a stream of equal payments
p: A monthly SIP, an EMI, rent, a pension: the same amount, every period. Excel calls it **pmt**, and the same five arguments still apply.
**pmt** is the regular payment; its sign follows the same rule: paying in is negative.
With monthly payments, the rate and nper are monthly too.
In finance this stream is an **annuity**, whatever it’s called on the bill.
In real life: started a ₹10,000 monthly SIP in an equity fund on her first salary day. Her question: what will 15 years of it be worth?

slides.h: Start or end of the period: type
p: SIPs and rent are paid at the **start** of each period, EMIs and salaries at the **end**. The last argument, **type**, says which: 1 for start, 0 (or left out) for end.
Each payment at the start earns one extra month of growth.
The difference here is about ₹50,000 on ₹50 lakh: worth getting right.
EMIs (Module 2) are paid at the end: type 0.
In real life: says rent is due on the 1st, in advance. To value five years of rent, his accountant uses type 1.

terms: 0 = payments at the end of each period (the default), 1 = at the start

check.q: Meera’s SIP goes in on the 1st of every month. Which type should FV use?

why.0: Type 0 is for payments at the end of each period, like EMIs.
why.3: The SIP is the payment, so pmt is needed.

slides.h: PMT: how much a month to reach a goal
p: To have ₹1 crore in 20 years at 12%, `=PMT(12%/12, 240, 0, 10000000, 1)` gives the monthly SIP, paid at the start of each month: about ₹10,009.
PMT finds the payment that turns pv into fv.
Its answer is negative (money you pay in), so put a minus in front to show it as a positive amount.
Already saved something? Put it in pv, as a negative number.
In real life: wanted ₹1 crore for retirement and assumed they’d need ₹40,000 a month. Starting at 30, with 25 years to go, PMT said about ₹5,300 at 12%.

p: Saving ₹15,000 a month at 10%, how long until Meera has ₹25 lakh? `=NPER(10%/12, -15000, 0, 2500000)`: 105 months, about 8.7 years.
NPER answers in **periods**: months here. Divide by 12 for years.
The payment and the target need opposite signs, or there’s no answer (#NUM!).
It rarely comes out whole; round up to the next month.
In real life: wants a ₹25 lakh down payment for a flat. NPER told her nine years at ₹15,000 a month, so she raised the SIP when her salary rose.

slides.h: RATE: what a plan really earns
p: A savings plan takes ₹50,000 a year for 10 years and pays ₹6,75,000 at the end. `=RATE(10, -50000, 0, 675000, 1)` says that’s 5.39% a year.
The brochure says “₹6.75 lakh for ₹5 lakh paid”: that sounds like 35%.
RATE spreads it over the years and the timing: under 5.4% a year.
Always turn a plan’s promise into a rate before comparing it with anything else.
In real life: was sold a plan like this at the bank counter. RATE showed him a fixed deposit would have paid more, and the deposit had no lock-in.

terms: finds the interest rate per period that makes the other four numbers fit

check.q: Which function tells you how many months it takes to reach a target with a fixed SIP?
check.explain: NPER finds the number of periods.

why.3: FV finds the amount at the end.

demo.intro: Value Meera’s SIP, size a SIP for a ₹1 crore goal, and test a savings plan with RATE.

frames.say: In **B5**, `=FV(B3/12,B4*12,-B2)`: 180 monthly payments of ₹10,000 at 1% a month. About ₹49.96 lakh.
SIPs go in at the start of the month, so add **type 1** in **B6**: `=FV(B3/12,B4*12,-B2,0,1)`. About ₹50.46 lakh.
For the ₹1 crore goal, `=-PMT(E3/12,E4*12,0,E2,1)` in **E6**: about ₹10,000 a month. The minus shows it as a positive amount.
In **H6**, `=RATE(H3,-H2,0,H4,1)`: the plan’s premiums at the start of each year, its payout at the end. Only 5.4% a year, less than a 7% deposit.

lab.intro: The **Savings** sheet has four of Meera’s questions. Use **FV**, **PMT**, **PV** and **RATE**; amounts should show as **positive** numbers.

cells.D6: Monthly SIP needed, at month start (₹)

tasks.prompt: In **B5**, work out what Meera’s SIP is worth after B4 years if she pays at the **end** of each month.
hints: The SIP is paid in, so pmt is -B2.

mistakes.msg: That puts the SIP in as pv, a single deposit. A payment every month goes in the third argument, pmt: FV(rate, nper, -B2).
Type 1 is for payments at the start of each month. This one pays at the end: leave type out (or use 0).

tasks.prompt: In **B6**, work out the same SIP paid at the **start** of each month.
hints: pv is 0, and type 1 means the start of each period.

mistakes.msg: That’s the month-end SIP again. Add pv 0 and type 1 for payments at the start of each month: FV(…, -B2, 0, 1).

tasks.prompt: In **B7**, work out how much Meera **pays in** altogether.
hints: The SIP times the number of months.

tasks.prompt: In **E6**, use **PMT** to find the monthly SIP, paid at the start of each month, that reaches the goal in E2. Show it as a positive amount.
hints: PMT(rate, nper, pv, fv, type): pv is 0 and fv is the goal.
PMT’s answer is negative; put a minus in front.

mistakes.msg: That puts the goal in as pv, money you have today. The goal is at the end: PMT(rate, nper, 0, E2, 1).
The SIP is paid at the start of each month: add type 1 as the last argument.

tasks.prompt: In **E12**, work out the savings Meera needs at retirement to draw E9 a month (at the end of each month) for E11 years, at E10.
hints: The income is a stream of payments to her: PV of an annuity.
Monthly rate E10/12, months E11*12, pmt is the income.

tasks.prompt: In **H6**, use **RATE** to find the yearly return the savings plan gives. Premiums are paid at the **start** of each year.
hints: Premiums are paid in (-H2); the payout comes back (H4); type 1.

mistakes.msg: #NUM! usually means the signs don’t make sense: the premiums are paid in (-H2) and the payout comes back (H4).
The premiums are paid at the start of each year: add type 1 as the last argument.

tasks.prompt: The plan returns about 5.4% a year. A bank deposit pays 7%. What should Meera conclude?
hints: Compare the rate, not the rupees.
₹6.75 lakh back for ₹5 lakh paid sounds big, but it takes 10 years.
tasks.explain: 5.4% a year is well below the deposit’s 7%. Turning a payout into a rate makes the comparison honest.
options: The plan wins: she gets ₹1.75 lakh more than she pays
The deposit pays more, and doesn’t lock her money in for 10 years

why.0: The extra ₹1.75 lakh comes over 10 years; as a yearly rate it’s below a deposit.
why.2: That’s exactly what RATE is for.

quiz.q: Which argument holds a regular monthly SIP?
quiz.explain: pmt is the payment made every period.

quiz.q: Rent is paid on the 1st of every month. Which type?
quiz.explain: Payments at the start of a period use type 1.
12 payments of 1,000 at 1% a month grow to 12,682.50.

quiz.q: Which function finds the SIP needed to reach a goal?
NPER returns #NUM!. What’s the most likely cause?
options: The payment and the target have the same sign
quiz.explain: Money in and money out need opposite signs, or no number of periods can work.

quiz.q: A plan: pay ₹1 lakh a year for 5 years, get ₹5.5 lakh after 5 years. Which formula gives its yearly return, premiums at the start of each year?
quiz.explain: RATE with the premiums negative, the payout positive and type 1.

points: A **pmt** every period makes an annuity: SIPs, EMIs, rent, pensions. Payments in are negative.
**type 1** for payments at the start of each period (SIPs, rent), **0** for the end (EMIs).
**PMT** finds the payment, **NPER** the time, **RATE** the return: turn every plan into a rate before you compare.
recap.cheat: =FV(r/12, years*12, -SIP, 0, 1) for a SIP; PMT, NPER and RATE solve for the rest.
